items.title: The BSO Meets AI, and Explores the Vitality of Classical Music Today | The Harvard Crimson
items.summary:
At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. Thus, alongside the MIT Media Lab, Machover has developed an audio AI that takes in the playing of the orchestra as input and produces live synthetic sounds that — as Machover puts it — “enhances” the orchestra. [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] The piece was divided into three movements. The first movement, “SMASH UP,” was, in Machover’s words, a “clash/crisis” without audible enhancement from the AI.

The second, “WAKE UP,” was an “awakening”: the AI slowly produced sound in response to various solo lines in the orchestra. Then the last movement, “STAND UP,” was a “depiction of democracy,” as the musicians and AI listened to one another and negotiated the final musical product.

items.title: SPS to tighten student tech policies this week for students in grades 3 to 5
items.summary:
SEATTLE — Seattle Public Schools (SPS) is tightening its technology rules for some students this week, adding new limits aimed at reducing distractions and curbing reliance on generative AI tools.

Superintendent Ben Shuldiner said that when he arrived in Seattle, it was clear the district had “steered too heavily into an overreliance of technology.” [...] Under the changes, students in grades three through five will have a one-hour daily cap on screen time. The limit includes activities such as watching a 10-minute educational video.

The district will also no longer allow iPads and laptops to be used as incentives or rewards. In addition, Seattle Public Schools is blocking access to Minecraft, YouTube and Gemini, programs Shuldiner said have been "abused." [...] RELATED | Seattle schools to cap elementary students' screen time, block unapproved AI tools

Parents have been asking the district to review how technology is used in classrooms, saying students are getting distracted or relying too heavily on generative AI tools.

items.title: Microsoft opens Imagine Cup to startups, and the new rules show how its AI strategy has changed – GeekWire
items.summary:
Changing AI requirements: The clearest example is the Imagine Cup rules for AI usage. In 2024, entrants had to build their products with “Microsoft and/or OpenAI” services. In 2025, they had to use at least one Microsoft AI service. In 2026, they had to use at least two Microsoft AI services.

For 2027, they can use any AI they want, as long as they use Microsoft’s Azure cloud. [...] As recently as 2024, student teams couldn’t have raised more than $50,000 in outside funding to compete. Under the new rules, final-round judges, whose scores determine all of the winners, will look for net revenue retention over the previous 12 months, six months of traction data, and a customer reference willing to be contacted. [...] It’s the latest step in a broader evolution of the Imagine Cup, and the implications go beyond the competition itself. Changes in the rules from 2024 to 2027 show how Microsoft and the tech industry are adjusting, year by year, to the realities of the AI era.

Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] The piece was divided into three movements. The first movement, “SMASH UP,” was, in Machover’s words, a “clash/crisis” without audible enhancement from the AI.

The second, “WAKE UP,” was an “awakening”: the AI slowly produced sound in response to various solo lines in the orchestra. Then the last movement, “STAND UP,” was a “depiction of democracy,” as the musicians and AI listened to one another and negotiated the final musical product.

    """Return the nth Fibonacci number using recursion.
